system_context.primary_system: Unbound sponsor operations (contributions, grants, charity monitoring, reconciliation, service)
system_context.context: Sponsor legal control (§4966(d)(2)), payment rails, custodians, IRS data, December seasonality, small operating staff
system_context.focus: Human labour per account and its drivers

outcome: Unbound's planning models compute $50 per account-year exception labour in the expected case (30 FTE at 100k accounts), $9 low, $546 high; the adversarial review rated "excessive operational overhead" Likely.
manifestations: 30 FTE_avg exception specialists in the expected case [S economic-model:40]
32 of 148 statements need counsel or CPA approval; independent reviewers required repeatedly (report 14:17)
economics loop running weekly, monthly and quarterly (report 14:17)

origin_network.origin: controls specified as human review where a deterministic rule would suffice
legally reserved sponsor discretion and SoD/independence duties
incomplete or late external data creating exceptions (feeds, IRS lists)
labour priced at $124.5k-$250k loaded per FTE [S/A]
December surge k on daily arrivals
minutes per exception m (45 expected, 135 stress) [A]

propagation: Informational gaps -> exceptions (e) -> human minutes (m) -> FTE via A*g*e*m/(60*H) -> fixed staffing sized for December, not average -> cost per account. Organizational propagation: every new control specified as "review" adds to e without a matching removal.

direct_observation: formula and parameter ranges are documented [S economic-model:14-41]
inference: minimum-touch reduces e for deterministic steps
gaps: no measured e, m, rework, displaced work

control_points: CP1 data completeness at intake (validation at capture; feed conformance) -- reduces e at origin
CP2 deterministic rules replacing review for low-discretion steps -- reduces e
CP3 AI evidence dossiers for remaining exceptions -- reduces m
CP4 roster/seasonal design -- reduces cost of residual e*m
CP5 removing per-account recurring obligations (UNB-XIN-ADV-001) -- removes work outright
control_point_ranking: CP5 > CP1 > CP2 > CP3 > CP4. CP5 and CP1 remove work at origin (high influence, high controllability, low cost); CP2 depends on counsel Q1 (lower controllability); CP3 has least confidence (EV-DAF-016 hypothesis that 30-70% of review effort remains); CP4 manages rather than removes. Heuristic ordering, no weights.
confidence: Low-Medium (model structure documented; every parameter assumed)
diagnostic_sufficiency: Sufficient for a reversible next action: instrument and run a bounded cohort. Not sufficient to size headcount or set prices on minimum-touch savings.
unknowns: measured e and m by decision type
next_responsible_action: Instrument e, m, rework and displaced work from first production day; enable automation per decision type with control floors in force.
prospective_outcome_hypothesis: Minimum-touch lowers human labour per account by a large factor without degrading control effectiveness.
claim_state: unsupported (plausible, no completed evidence capable of testing it)
evidence_boundary: EDF v0.3 is a working grammar; control-point quality, reproducibility and value beyond neutral structure are not established (EDF README:17-35). Same-model analysis; Diagnostic Calibration not performed.

recommendation: Exploratory per-account cost targets and small-balance viability

system_context.context: Fee revenue on small balances, fund-borne investment and custody costs, payment rails, structural staffing
system_context.focus: Why small accounts are modelled as unprofitable and what could change that

outcome: Unbound's models give $244-$272 fully allocated cost per account-year; a $1,000 fund at 1% yields $10/yr; release 1 excludes the high-volume/low-balance model.

origin_network.origin: asset-based fee on small balances yields single-digit dollars
fixed and step-fixed costs (SoD roster, counsel/CPA, December specialists) allocated per account
per-account recurring obligations (attestations, recertification, statements, acknowledgments)
custody and payment per-account/per-item costs ($14.40 custody in the example)
cost denominators not separated: per account vs per grant vs per dollar

propagation: Financial: fixed and per-account costs / low revenue per small account -> negative contribution. Informational: a single fully allocated average hides that marginal cost of an extra DigitalMinimal account may be far lower than the average, or higher if small accounts generate more exceptions.

inference: $10 fully allocated at 100k accounts = $1.0m total = 6.1-8.0 FTE at $124.5k-$165k with zero other cost [D]
gaps: no marginal cost curve by balance band
no exception rate by balance band

control_points: CP1 servicing class with per-account obligation budget (UNB-XIN-ADV-001)
CP2 pricing/fee floor (XID-ECO-002)
CP3 cost-layer separation: fund-borne vs sponsor vs platform
CP4 exception rate for small accounts
CP5 scale (fixed-cost dilution)
control_point_ranking: CP3 first (it is a definitional fix that makes every other control measurable, near-zero cost, high confidence); then CP1 (high influence, controllable by sponsor policy); CP2 (high influence, constrained by counsel reasonableness and donor fairness); CP4 (unknown magnitude); CP5 (low controllability).
confidence: Medium for "small accounts are unprofitable under current requirements"; Low for any specific target value
diagnostic_sufficiency: Sufficient to restate the targets by layer and scale and to keep HVLB out of release 1. Not sufficient to publish fee floors or commit to $10.
unknowns: exception and fraud rate by balance band
next_responsible_action: Restate the ladder as layer- and scale-specific hypotheses; measure cost per account-month by balance band in release 1.
prospective_outcome_hypothesis: Per-account cost can be driven to $10 and small balances served viably.
claim_state: unsupported for $10 fully allocated (contradicted by documented component costs, see SPF-CLR-002); unsupported for $10 marginal
evidence_boundary: EDF v0.3 is a working grammar; control-point quality, reproducibility and value beyond neutral structure are not established (EDF README:17-35). Same-model analysis; Diagnostic Calibration not performed.

system_context.primary_system: Unbound transactional core (ledger, reservations, holds, outbox, process managers)
system_context.context: Managed PostgreSQL, per-sponsor databases, platform hold registry, external batch truth
system_context.focus: Whether the hybrid architecture holds invariants at peak load and under failure

outcome: On a single 4-vCPU VM the benchmark sustained 2,100-3,944 tx/s with 0 failures and p99 approval <=41 ms at 200 tx/s; a single-transaction fee batch raised approval p99 to 244 ms (max 347 ms).

origin_network.origin: row-lock contention on fund rows held by long transactions
cross-database hold check (HoldPublicationVersion) without a shared transaction
hand-written process managers maintained by a small team
managed-storage commit latency (not measured)

propagation: Physical/technical: long batch -> fund-row locks -> approval latency (measured). Informational: registry unavailable -> every sponsor's releases blocked (fail closed; not measured). Organizational: defect in one process manager -> stuck workflows -> manual recovery load on few people.

inference: managed DB will be slower but within headroom (RTT scenario suggests 2,127 tx/s)

control_points: CP1 chunked batches (adopted)
CP2 registry placement and fail-closed behaviour with availability objective
CP3 managed-DB re-benchmark
CP4 recovery drill (PITR + process manager resume)
CP5 limit long-running workflow types (criterion 6)
control_point_ranking: CP2 > CP4 > CP3 > CP5 > CP1 (CP1 done). CP2 has highest influence on availability across sponsors and is cheap to decide (co-locate for release 1); CP4 tests the minimum-touch dependency on automated recovery; CP3 is required before production but expected to pass by an order of magnitude.
confidence: Medium-High for throughput and serialization within a sponsor; Low for cross-database and recovery behaviour
diagnostic_sufficiency: Sufficient to adopt ADR-EVA-001 for release 1 and to reject a broker, event store, workflow engine or service split. Not sufficient for multi-sponsor production with a separate registry database.
next_responsible_action: Decide registry co-location for release 1 (SPD-ARX-001); run the benchmarks in "Theoretical benchmarks and acceptance scenarios".
prospective_outcome_hypothesis: The hybrid architecture remains sufficient without distributed components through multi-sponsor scale.
claim_state: suggestive (one environment, explicit limits; within-condition measurement, not cross-condition reproduction)
evidence_boundary: EDF v0.3 is a working grammar; control-point quality, reproducibility and value beyond neutral structure are not established (EDF README:17-35). Same-model analysis; Diagnostic Calibration not performed.

recommendation: Continuous charity monitoring with automatic approval and exception review

system_context.primary_system: Charity eligibility monitoring and Tier-1 grant approval
system_context.context: IRS publications (Pub 78/BMF/auto-revocation), sanctions lists, shared platform registry, sponsor board delegation, payment settlement
system_context.focus: How an ineligible payment could occur under automated monitoring

outcome: Requirements specify two-point eligibility checks with fail-closed holds; report 12 records two unhandled paths: a revocation not yet ingested and a payment already transmitted.
manifestations: XDS adversarial outcome "Not handled if the revocation has not yet been ingested" (report 12 §6)

origin_network.origin: IRS publication latency and list semantics
ingestion latency and source outages
settlement irreversibility of rails
freshness window and deep-review interval set by sponsor policy
sampling reviewers and rule owners (detective layer)

propagation: Informational: source change -> publication delay -> ingestion delay -> stale reliance snapshot -> release passes -> payment settles (financial, irreversible) -> post-payment remediation (UNB-XIN-NPG-008). Organizational: false-positive holds -> complaints -> pressure to widen windows -> larger stale window.
control_points: CP1 freshness watermark gate (EVA-004 + RR-REQ-X-007-r1 AC-4)
CP2 release-time re-check and dispatcher re-check (EVA-011)
CP3 freshness window value
CP4 decision-quality sampling (CLM-005)
CP5 post-payment remediation workflow (NPG-008)
control_point_ranking: CP1 > CP2 > CP3 > CP4 > CP5: preventive gates at release have highest influence and are deterministic; CP3 is a policy dial with Trigger-Drift risk; CP4 is detective and labour-bearing; CP5 recovers only part of the loss.
confidence: Medium (control design explicit; data behaviour unmeasured)
diagnostic_sufficiency: Sufficient to keep the design and to enable automated clean refreshes. Not sufficient to enable Tier-1 approval in production before counsel Q1 and source latency measurement.
next_responsible_action: Measure source latency; budget sampling; obtain counsel Q1; then enable Tier-1 per rule version with monitoring triggers (RR-UNB-GRANT-030-r1).
prospective_outcome_hypothesis: Automated monitoring with exception review prevents ineligible payments at lower cost than routine human vetting.
evidence_boundary: EDF v0.3 is a working grammar; control-point quality, reproducibility and value beyond neutral structure are not established (EDF README:17-35). Same-model analysis; Diagnostic Calibration not performed.

system_context.context: Platform counsel/CPA review, sponsor exclusive legal control, multi-sponsor future

outcome: The adversarial review found at least 14 versioned registers per sponsor database with no defaults and rated configuration complexity Likely to cause failure; report 12 lists correlated pack misconfiguration as a residual risk.

origin_network.origin: jurisdiction- and rail-specific obligations
per-sponsor approval of every register
one-database-per-sponsor multiplies configuration instances
shared pack authored once for all sponsors

propagation: Per-sponsor configuration -> onboarding load and divergent errors (many small, independent). Shared pack -> one error -> every adopting sponsor at the same effective date (few, correlated, larger blast radius).

inference: packs shift error distribution from independent to correlated

control_points: CP1 staged rollout with lag between sponsors
CP2 cross-sponsor shadow evaluation of each pack version on historical decisions
CP3 per-parameter ordering ("tighter") or enumerated alternatives
CP4 deviation workflow via sponsor counsel
control_point_ranking: CP2 > CP1 > CP3 > CP4: CP2 detects before any live effect; CP1 bounds blast radius; CP3 removes ambiguity at low cost; CP4 is the existing exception path.
diagnostic_sufficiency: Sufficient to adopt packs for one sponsor and to require CP1/CP2 before the second sponsor.
unknowns: who is liable for pack content
prospective_outcome_hypothesis: Default packs reduce configuration cost without raising aggregate error cost.

system_context.primary_system: Legal and accounting basis of platform defaults
system_context.context: Counsel, external CPA, auditor, IRS, payment networks, state regulators
system_context.focus: How provisional positions propagate into built behaviour

outcome: All 41 questions are decided-provisional by an AI integrator at the owner's direction; 46 records adopted into domain files; verification of a subset changed at least four positions; 2 of 11 legal claims failed a spot check.

origin_network.origin: owner direction to decide in order to unblock design
authority partly general knowledge (FASB Codification not read)
single model family produced, reviewed and adopted
genuinely unsettled questions (money transmission, AB 488, ASC 958 variance power)

propagation: Informational/organizational: provisional decision -> adopted requirement -> design -> code -> issued artifacts (acknowledgments, statements, journals) -> irreversible external effects. Each step raises the cost of a later counsel/CPA reversal.

inference: unverified items likely contain errors at a rate comparable to verified ones

control_points: CP1 production activation gate on confirmation status (UNB-SMP-CLR-002, proposed)
CP2 dependency-ordered confirmation plan
CP3 versioned, switchable behaviour for each decision
CP4 dated human owner per decision
control_point_ranking: CP1 > CP3 > CP2 > CP4. CP1 stops propagation at the irreversible boundary; CP3 preserves correctability; CP2 reduces time-at-risk; CP4 fixes ownership.
confidence: High that the decisions are provisional and unvalidated (narrow methodological claim); Low-Medium on their correctness as a set
diagnostic_sufficiency: Sufficient to continue design under the decisions. Not sufficient to activate any affected behaviour in production.
next_responsible_action: Machine-enforce provisional status; order confirmations by downstream dependency and irreversibility.
prospective_outcome_hypothesis: The provisional decisions will be largely confirmed and require only wording changes.
